videos.caption: Crispy tortilla cones filled with juicy spiced beef and topped with melted mozzarella 🧀🔥 The perfect crunchy snack or quick dinner that everyone will love. One bite and you’re hooked 🤤 Crispy Beef Cones (12 cones) Ingredients For the cones:  • 6 tortillas (25–30 cm / 10–12 inches)  • Toothpicks For the topping:  • Mozzarella cheese, 100 g  • Chopped parsley, 1 tsp For the beef mixture:  • Ground beef, 400 g(0.8lb)   • 1 yellow onion, finely chopped  • Garlic, 4 cloves, minced  • Red bell pepper, diced (about 1 small)  • Green bell pepper, diced (about 1 small)  • Tomato paste, 1 big tbsp   • Soy milk, 100 ml (~ ½ cup) Seasoning:  • Paprika, 1 tbsp  • Chili powder, 1 tsp  • Turmeric, 1 tsp  • Garlic powder, 1 tsp  • Black pepper, 1 tsp  • Garam masala, 1 tsp  • Salt, ½ tsp Instructions 1.⁠ ⁠Prepare the beef mixture:  • Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until soft.  • Add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.  • Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.  • Stir in tomato paste, soy milk, diced bell peppers, and all seasonings. Cook until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. 2.⁠ ⁠Prepare the cones:  • Cut tortillas in half. Roll each half into a cone shape and secure the edge with a toothpick. Baking Method:  1. Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).  2. Place cones on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Lightly spray with cooking spray.  3. Bake for 10–12 minutes until crispy and golden.  4. Fill each cone with the beef mixture and top with mozzarella cheese.  5. Return to oven for 5 minutes until cheese melts.  6. Garnish with parsley and serve warm. Air Fryer Method:   1. Preheat air fryer to 180°C (356°F).  2. Lightly spray cones with cooking spray and place them in the air fryer basket. Make sure they don’t touch each other.  3. Air fry for 6–8 minutes until crispy and golden.  4. Carefully fill each cone with the beef mixture and top with mozzarella cheese.  5. Air fry again for 3–4 minutes until cheese melts.  6. Garnish with parsley and serve warm. #crispybeef #quickrecipes #easyrecipes #lazydinner #beefcones

HOW TO MAKE SALT BREAD 🥐 i wanted to answer some of the questions i was getting about my salt bread recipe so i wanted to make a longer more in depth tutorial recipe link: https://erinscozykitchen.com/recipe/salt-bread-shiopan/ or look up "erinscozykitchen salt bread" on google and it should be the first link that pops up! - can i replace milk powder with milk: yes you can just replace some or all the water with milk but it will change the crumb and texture and browning, if u can i would recommend using milk powder - why cold water: when you knead your dough it will rise the temp and you want it to end up at around 78 fahrenheit when u go to do the first rise. high dough temp will affect the taste and gluten development of the dough - why is my dough sticky: your dough has either gotten too high in temp that the gluten is breaking down or you haven't kneaded it long enough and it's just underdeveloped (DONT add more flour to your dough just bc it's sticky while you're kneading it shouldn't need any flour if you kneaded it long enough). i have made these hundreds of times and i promise if you knead it long enough even if it takes a while it will come together eventually and get less sticky! if you have tried all these steps and the dough is still too difficult to work with you can try changing the unsalted butter amount to 30g instead of 40g. My current recipe is on the higher side of fat content which is why it takes a longer time to knead and for the dough to come together. if you use 30g it should come together faster and be easier to manage but will still taste good!  - how long do you knead: this depends on your mixer and speed, with my ooni halo pro it took me about 14 min total but with a kitchen aid it could take longer and by hand even longer  - where is my salt bread pan from: i got it in korea at bangsan market! it's a neighborhood that sells a lot of wholesale baking and packaging supplies. i couldn't find anything similar in the states but tbh i don't think it really makes that big of a difference! tips: • make sure you fridge your butter after you cut it, you want to roll it up with hard/cold sticks of butter • for cute fat salt bread make the top width of your rolled out inverted triangle short • start preheating your oven around 25 min after your final shaping while they're rising so they're not overproofed by the time your oven is ready • make sure to use a nonstick coated baking pan for your rolls! a plain aluminum pan will cause your rolls to stick it needs to be non stick coated :)  STORAGE • salt bread tastes best fresh out of the oven! if you don't finish them freeze them in a ziploc and to reheat, air fry at 350 f for 5-8 min #saltbread #shiopan #소금빵

Creamy Tuscan Chicken 🍗✨ This creamy Tuscan chicken is packed with juicy seasoned chicken, garlic, spinach, and sweet grape tomatoes in a rich Parmesan cream sauce. It’s perfect served over pasta, mashed potatoes, or rice! 😋  🍗 Creamy Tuscan Chicken Ingredients:  Chicken seasoning  * 2 to 3 chicken breasts, sliced in half * Salt & pepper * ½ tsp smoked paprika * 1 tsp garlic powder * 1 tbsp Italian seasoning * 1 tsp dried parsley * ½ tsp chili flakes (optional) Sauce: * 1 tbsp butter * ½ onion, diced * 3 garlic cloves, minced * 1 cup grape tomatoes, halved * 2 cups spinach * 1 cup heavy cream * ¼ cup grated Parmesan * Salt & pepper, to taste * Fresh parsley Directions: Season the chicken with all the spices. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a skillet and cook the chicken for 4–5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside. In the same skillet, melt the butter and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and cook for 2–3 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted. Pour in the heavy cream and Parmesan, stirring until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Return the chicken to the skillet and let simmer for 2–3 minutes. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve over pasta, mashed potatoes, or rice. Enjoy! 🤍

Blueberry pull apart bread 🫐✨ Ingredients  Bread - 435g bread flour (3 cups + 2 tbsp) - 68g granulated sugar (1/3 cup) - 185g whole milk (3/4 cup) - 60g unsalted butter, softened (4 tbsp) - 7g active dry yeast (2 1/4 tsp) - 2 large eggs - 1/2 tsp salt Blueberry compote - 300g blueberries (about 2 cups) - 95g granulated sugar (10 tbsp + 2 tsp) - 1 tbsp lemon juice  - 12g cornstarch (cornstarch slurry) - 2 tbsp water (cornstarch slurry) Icing (didn’t measure) - Confectioners sugar - Melted butter - Whole milk - Splash of vanilla extract  - Splash of lemon extract  Instructions  Filling - In a medium sauce pan on medium heat combine blueberries, sugar, and lemon juice. Stir until well combined and cook until bubbling. - Add cornstarch slurry and stir constantly until very thick.  - Transfer into a heat safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and cool for 10 minutes on the counter then refrigerate for 30-40 minutes. Bread - In a bowl, combine warm milk and 1 tbsp sugar. Sprinkle yeast over the top, stir lightly, and let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy. - Add eggs, 1/3 sugar, and mix again until well combined. - Add flour to mixture. Mix until a rough dough forms. - Begin kneading. Once the dough starts to come together, gradually add the softened butter (1 tbsp at a time), kneading until fully incorporated before adding more. - Continue kneading 8–10 minutes by hand or 5–6 minutes in a stand mixer, until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky. - Transfer dough to a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1–1½ hours, or until doubled in size. - Punch down dough and roll into a rectangle about 12x18 inches - Spread filling evenly across the surface - Cut into strips, then stack and cut again to fit upright into a greased loaf pan (1/2 pound loaf pan) - Cover loosely and let rise 30–40 minutes, until puffy. - Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 35–40 minutes, tenting with foil if the top browns too quickly. - Top with icing and serve!  • • • #recipes #baking #springrecipes #bakingrecipe #recipeideas

RECIPE Toffee: - 1/2 cup unsalted butter - 1 cup light brown sugar - Pinch of salt  Cookie dough:  - 2 cups all purpose flour - 1 1/2 tsp salt - 1 tsp baking soda - 1 cup unsalted butter, melted - 2 tbsp room temp water - 1 cup dark brown sugar  - 1/2 cup white sugar - 1 tsp vanilla extract - 1/2 rounded tsp espresso powder  - 1 large egg - 1 egg yolk - 1 1/2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chunks - 1/2 dark chocolate chunks  - 1 cup toffee bits 1. Make the toffee: combine butter and brown sugar in a saucepan. Place over medium heat. Allow butter to melt and whisk together to combine with the sugar. Bring to a bubble, whisking consistently. Use a candy thermometer and wait for the mixture to reach 300F (about 8 minutes) then remove from heat and pour onto a silicone or parchment lined baking sheet. Quickly spread the mixture out with a spatula to an smooth slab. Let cool for 20 minutes until hardened. Break toffee apart into small pieces as desired.   2. For the cookies: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook over a medium heat until the milk solids have browned and the butter is a nutty brown color. Transfer to a Pyrex cup, and add the water to make the liquids equal to 1 cup. Allow to cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes.  3. In the meantime, in a small bowl mix together the flour, salt and baking soda. Set aside.  4. In a large bowl, combine the brown and white sugars with the brown butter, and whisk together vigorously to combine. Once homogenous, add the vanilla extract and espresso powder. Whisk to combine. Next, add the egg and egg yolk, whisk to combine.  5. Add the dry ingredients to the wet, and mix gently with a spatula to combine, stopping once you see no more streaks of flour and a dough has formed.  6. Add the chocolate and toffee bits and mix once more to combine.  7. Use a 3 tbsp cookie scoop to portion the cookie dough onto a lined plate or baking sheet. It should yield about 14 cookies. Cover and place in the freezer for at least 3 hours or overnight.  8. When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 350F and bake cookies for 15 minutes. Once golden brown, remove from oven. Transfer to a cooling rack after 5 minutes and sprinkle with flakey salt. For misshapen cookies, use a round cup or bowl to gently reform into a circle. Allow to cool and enjoy! I’ll also put the recipe below!!🎄🩷  - A note on rise times to ensure maximum fluffiness: make sure to allow the dough to fully proof before baking, especially during the 2nd proof. My house/ environment is very warm so these rise super quickly but if your house is cold right now then you need to create a warmer environment for them to properly rise - you can put them in the oven with the oven light on, or in the microwave after heating up a cup of water for a few minutes, or with a heating pad on low that's wrapped in a towel (we don't want to get the dough hot, just slightly warm). Just make sure they look nice & big & fluffy before baking, & if they're not then let them keep rising. —- Salted Honey Butter Rolls  (with sourdough discard) . Ingredients: Makes 15 extra large rolls or 24 regular sized rolls . For the dough (sourdough version) 690g flour 245g water (warm if your house is cold) 300g sourdough starter or discard 18g yeast 2 large eggs 105g honey (or sugar) 56g salted butter, softened 2.5 tsp salt (12g) . Non-Sourdough Version: If you’re *not* using sourdough discard, increase the flour to 840g total and the water to 395g water total but keep every other measurement the same.  Optional egg wash to brush on top of the rolls: -   1 egg -  about 1 TBSP milk or cream (I found that cream with a splash of water works best) —- Instructions 1. To make the dough: Combine all dough ingredients except for the butter in the bowl of a stand mixer. Mix on low speed for a minute or two until the flour is all absorbed, then mix on high or medium high speed for about 10 minutes until you have a soft, smooth dough that is close to passing the windowpane test. At this point you can add the softened butter and mix for a few more minutes until all combined. The dough should be smooth, strong, and slightly shiny. Shape it into a ball in the mixing bowl and cover. Let rise until it's nearly doubled in size, about 1 to 2 hours.  2. To shape the buns: Gently deflate the dough and divide into 15-24 rolls depending on the size you want. In the video I made 15 extra large rolls that were each about 105 grams. For a more standard size, measure each roll out to about 63g (this will make 24 rolls). Shape each piece into a ball. It will be very sticky but just divide, the plop on a clean surface and start shaping. To smooth it out, cup your hands and pull the dough ball towards you to tighten the outer layer and create a smooth, round dough ball. Place buns on a lightly greased parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover and let rise until light and puffy, about an hour to 1.5 hours (but possibly more, see not above for tips on proof times). Toward the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 375°F. 3. Make the egg wash: This is optional, but for that extra golden shine on top of your buns, make an egg wash by mixing one egg with a splash of milk or cream. I actually prefer to do a splash of cream with a small splash of water. Mix until you have one cohesive liquid, then brush over the buns before baking. Now sprinkle with coarse sea salt if you'd like (highly recommend). 4. To bake the buns: If you the buns are small, bake for about 16-18 minutes, until golden. For large buns around 100g, you'll need to bake a little bit longer, for about 25 minutes, or until the middle of a roll reads 190F on a thermometer. If you make the XL ones you can take the out when a roll in the center of the pan is getting close to 185F since it will continue to cook a little bit once you take it out. If your rolls are getting too dark, you can turn down the oven temp a little bit during the last 10 minutes. Optional: once they're out of the oven, brush with melted butter or just rub a cold stick of butter over the top of the rolls and it will melt onto them. This will give them a satiny, buttery crust. Garlic parmesan japanese long fries 🍟  Ingredients  4 large russet potatoes  1/2 cup cornstarch Salt to taste 1 tbsp garlic powder 1 tsp black pepper  Avocado Oil for frying  For garnish  1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese  1 tbsp freshly chopped parsley For the garlic parmesan mayonnaise: 1/2 cup mayonnaise 2 garlic cloves, finely grated 2 tbsp freshly grated Parmesan cheese 1 tsp lemon juice 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/4 tsp black pepper Salt to taste 1 tsp olive oil 1–2 tsp water, if needed, to thin Method: Boil the potatoes until completely tender. Drain very well. Mash while they're hot. Add the cornstarch, black pepper, salt, garlic powder. Mix until you have a thick, smooth, moldable dough If the dough feels sticky or soft, add another 5–10 g corn starch. It should be firm enough to hold a shape. Once the potato dough is prepared, place it on a sheet of parchment paper. Cover the dough with another sheet of parchment paper and use a rolling pin to roll it out into an even rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick. Remove the top parchment paper and use a sharp knife or pizza cutter to cut the dough into long, even strips. Gently separate the strips and place them on a parchment-lined tray. Chill the potato strips for 30 minutes to firm them up before frying. Add the mayonnaise, grated garlic, Parmesan, lemon juice, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and olive oil to a bowl. Mix until completely smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust the salt, lemon, or garlic according to your preference.If you want a thinner dipping sauce, mix in 1–2 teaspoons of water. Heat oil to 350°F (175°C). Carefully place the chilled potato strips into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan or move them for the first 60 seconds, allowing the outside to set. Fry for 3–4 minutes, turning gently, until golden brown and crisp. Remove and drain on a wire rack or paper towels.  Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and parsley. Cowboy Butter Cheeseburger Sliders These Cowboy Butter Cheeseburger Sliders are cheesy, buttery, and packed with flavor! Perfect for an easy dinner, game day, or feeding a crowd! Ingredients For the Sliders 1 lb ground beef ½ yellow onion, diced 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce ½ tsp garlic powder ½ tsp onion powder 1 tsp cowboy butter seasoning, or to taste 1 package sliced provolone cheese ⅓ cup French fried onions 1 package slider buns (12 count) 2 tbsp mayonnaise 1 tbsp Dijon mustard For the Cowboy Butter Topping 2 tbsp butter, melted 2 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped ½ tsp cowboy butter seasoning Directions 1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. 2. Add the ground beef and diced onion to a large skillet over medium heat. Cook, until the meat is fully cooked and the onion is tender. Drain any excess grease. 3. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, and cowboy butter seasoning. 4. Add 4 slices of provolone cheese and the French fried onions to the beef mixture. Cover the skillet with a lid and allow the cheese to melt. Stir everything together until creamy and combined. 5. Slice the entire package of slider buns in half horizontally. Place the bottom half in a baking dish. 6. In a small bowl, mix together the mayonnaise and Dijon mustard. Spread the mixture evenly over the bottom buns. 7. Add a layer of provolone cheese over the buns, followed by the cheeseburger mixture. Top with the remaining provolone cheese. 8. Place the top half of the slider buns over the cheese. 9. In a small bowl, combine the melted butter, fresh parsley, and ½ teaspoon cowboy butter seasoning. Brush generously over the tops of the sliders. 10. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake at 400°F for 20–25 minutes, or until the sliders are heated through and the cheese is completely melted. 11. Remove the foil and, if desired, bake for another 2–3 minutes to lightly toast the tops. 12. Slice into individual sliders and serve warm. Enjoy! #easyrecipe #dinnerideas #quickrecipes #easydinner #sliders
